newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia MoF seeks tighter grip on govt debt market.
newsitem.headline: Russia MoF seeks tighter grip on govt debt market.

text.p: The Russian Finance Ministry has worked out a draft system to control the government securities market more tightly, Finance Minister Alexander Livshits told a news conference on Friday.

"We are talking about a more active Finance Ministry role on the market," Livshits said. "We shall change the structure of the market in favour of longer-term paper, minimise the cost of borrowing and provide for the possibility of substituting domestic borrowing for international borrowing."
He said the finance ministry would set up special reserve funds under the draft system. This would allow the ministry to be a player on the domestic government debt market.

Currently the central bank, the Finance Ministry's agent on the market, buys GKO discount Treasury bills and OFZ interest-bearing bonds on the secondary market. It also organises occasional Lombard auctions to regulate liquidity on the market.

T-bill yields have been falling steadily to the current 30 percent annual from about 200 percent in the summer, partly due to lower inflation and partly because Russia has boosted access to foreign investors and the higher demand has pushed yields down.
